common_footer: Work only inside `concierge-agent/`. Finish this step by running `node --check` on every module you touched and then `bash gate.sh` (the test runner); fix what fails. Do not start the server, do not install browsers, do not contact any live service.

turns.prompt: E1.1 — Read every entry point, request handler and outbound call in `concierge-agent/` (server.mjs, agent.mjs, classify.mjs, qa.mjs, qa-corpus.mjs, train.mjs, trends_sync.py). List every unhandled-error surface as `file:line — what can throw — what happens today`. Write the list to `concierge-agent/ERRORS.md`. No code changes in this step.

E1.2 — Add a typed error hierarchy in a new module `concierge-agent/errors.mjs`: an `AppError` base with `code`, `kind` (one of network / auth / booking / llm / unknown), `cause`, and `toJSON()`; one subclass per kind. Add process-level `uncaughtException` and `unhandledRejection` handlers (in a module the server imports at startup) that log a structured JSON line and never let the process die silently. Wrap the surfaces you listed in ERRORS.md so they raise `AppError`s.

E1.3 — Add structured error reporting to Supabase in `concierge-agent/report.mjs`: every `AppError` is reported with service name, version, kind, code, timestamp and a message with NO personal data (no names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, intent payloads). Use an existing table if one fits, otherwise define a new table in a migration file `concierge-agent/migrations/0001_error_reports.sql`. Batch reports and retry with exponential backoff; never block a request on reporting.

E1.4 — Write tests (node:test, files named `*.test.mjs` next to the code) for the error hierarchy, the process-level handlers and the reporter (batching, backoff, PII scrubbing). Mock the network; nothing may reach a live service. Make the whole test runner green.

E2.1 — Security audit of `concierge-agent/`: grep for secrets, tokens, keys, hardcoded URLs, service-role usage and anything that would leak on a log line. Write the findings to `concierge-agent/SECURITY_AUDIT.md` as `file:line — finding — severity`. No code changes in this step.

E2.2 — Add `concierge-agent/config.mjs` that loads every configuration value from the environment, validates it at startup (types, required, URL shape) and fails fast with an `AppError` of kind auth or unknown naming the missing key (never its value). Replace every direct `process.env` read in the modules with the config module.

E2.3 — Validate every inbound payload server-side (the webhook body, the reconcile request, anything parsed from a request or from Supabase rows before it is trusted): schema-check in `concierge-agent/validate.mjs`, reject with 400 and an `AppError` on failure. Then review Supabase row-level security for every table this agent reads or writes: list each exact table name and the RLS gap you see in `concierge-agent/RLS_REVIEW.md`, and fix what is fixable from this repo (a migration file under `concierge-agent/migrations/`).

E2.4 — Run `npm audit` in `concierge-agent/` (it may fail without a lockfile or network; record what it printed in `SECURITY_AUDIT.md`). Pin every dependency in package.json to an exact version, with one line of reason per change in `SECURITY_AUDIT.md`. Keep the test runner green.

E3.1 — Wrap every outbound call (Supabase queries, the admin edge function, Telegram, the agent SDK, the discovery endpoints) in `concierge-agent/outbound.mjs` with a per-call timeout, jittered exponential-backoff retry for retryable failures only, and classification of every failure into an `AppError` kind.

E3.2 — Add idempotency keys to every booking or payment write (confirm, reject, route_to_owner, and any insert that money or a calendar depends on): derive the key from the intent id and action, persist it, and make a replayed request a no-op that returns the first result.

E3.3 — Add an ordered outbound message queue in `concierge-agent/queue.mjs` for Telegram and reporting sends: FIFO per destination, persisted to disk under `concierge-agent/.queue/`, `flush()` on shutdown, and a dead-letter file for messages that exhaust their retries.

E3.4 — Add a circuit breaker in `concierge-agent/breaker.mjs` (closed / open / half-open with a cool-down) around Supabase and around the LLM/agent path, and graceful degradation when either is open: intents are routed to the owner with a clear admin note instead of failing. Tests for breaker, queue, idempotency and outbound retry; test runner green.

E4.1 — Create one LLM client module `concierge-agent/llm.mjs` used by every LLM step. It runs the model through the local `claude -p` command on the machine's Max OAuth session (spawn `claude -p <prompt> --output-format json`; assume NO API key and never skip or stub the LLM step in production paths). Give it the circuit breaker, a per-request cost guard (from the JSON result's cost field; refuse over a configurable ceiling), structured JSON outputs with schema validation, and static fallback copy when the breaker is open or the guard trips.

E4.2 — Route concierge replies through `llm.mjs`: chunk long replies, persist conversation state (per intent id) to disk under `concierge-agent/.state/` so a restart resumes mid-conversation, and expose the reply path as a function the server can call.

E4.3 — Add a proactive suggestion generator `concierge-agent/suggest.mjs`: from recent user activity (recent intents and messages for a user), produce one suggestion through `llm.mjs`; cache per user for a configurable TTL, rate-limit per user, and let a suggestion be dismissed so it is not shown again.

E4.4 — Every user-facing `AppError` message is rewritten by `llm.mjs` into plain language with one concrete next step, with a static fallback and never leaking internals (no stack, no table names, no keys). Add a smart retry: when a retryable failure happens, the agent explains in one sentence what it will try next, then does it.

E4.5 — Tests for the breaker, the cost guard, the fallback copy and one end-to-end path (webhook in → classify → outbound with mocks → reply out). Then write `concierge-agent/HANDOFF.md`: for each of E1–E4 and each numbered step, mark done / partial / not started with one line of evidence (file or test name). Test runner green.
